title: Compact-support calculus on varying coefficient towers
statement:
Work with separated finite-type schemes over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Use the category $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], and its full ordinary derived subcategory $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ with uniformly bounded cohomological and Tor intervals [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Normalization is not assumed. At finite levels the coefficient category is the ordinary module derived category over the constant finite ring $A_n$, with bounded intrinsically constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. For a separated finite-type map $h:T\to B$ choose a compactification $h=\bar h\circ j$ and put $F_h=R\bar h_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$, with its finite evaluations as in [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Write $F_{h,n}=Rh_{!,A_n}$. Assume $F_h(\mathcal C_T)\subseteq\mathcal C_B$ for each map at which this restriction is used.

(1) For composable maps $T\xrightarrow h B\xrightarrow g C$ there is a natural isomorphism of exact functors
$$\alpha_{g,h}:F_gF_h\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gh}$$
on these categories. It is compatible with compactification refinement, identities and associativity, and evaluation at $n$ is the canonical finite compact-support composition isomorphism. For an open immersion $u:U\hookrightarrow T$, its normalization is $F_{hu}=F_hu_{!,\bullet}$ with the canonical open-extension counits.

(2) If $e:U\to T$ is separated, etale and of finite type, then $F_e=e_{!,\bullet}$ on $\mathcal C_U$, where $e_{!,\bullet}$ is the exact, levelwise sheaf extension along the localized pro-etale sites. It is left adjoint to exact levelwise inverse image $e_\bullet^*$, also on the ordinary derived categories. At finite levels its counit is the sum over the geometric fibres. Both functors preserve constructibility and uniform cohomological and Tor intervals. These adjunction maps evaluate to the finite ones and are compatible with the coefficient quotient maps. The open-immersion case is extension by zero.

(3) Write $r^C_{n,m}:C_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\to C_m$ for the reduction map of a tower [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], $m\leq n$. Under the finite evaluations of $F_h$, its reduction map is
$$r^{F_hC}_{n,m}=F_{h,m}(r^C_{n,m})\circ b_h(C_n),$$
where $b_h(C_n):(F_{h,n}C_n)\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h,m}(C_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m)$ is the canonical coefficient-extension comparison of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. This identity is natural in $C$ and compatible with compositions of quotient maps. In this normalization the proper part of $b_h$ is the $A_m$-linear adjoint transpose of the $A_n$-counit after scalar extension, followed by the canonical extension-by-zero tensor comparison, as specified in [det-sp-reduction-direct-image].

proof.text: Use the actual strict semilinear section model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] with ring system $A_{n,T}$: its ordinary homotopy category is $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$, and it supplies inverse image, separately derived direct image, open extension, their units/counits, and the comparisons built from them. It does not identify a derived morphism with an arbitrary family of its evaluations. Every level of an object of $\mathcal C_T$ has bounded constructible etale origin by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. These representatives have the same Tor intervals by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]: the schemes are qcqs and $A_n$ is finite, hence discrete Noetherian. Consequently the finite comparisons in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] apply over the arbitrary field $k$ in the statement; no global finite-field datum is needed. We will use [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] to identify evaluations and detect invertibility only after constructing maps in the section model.

proof.text:
Construct proper/open comparisons before evaluation. For a commutative square $pk=ir$ with $p,r$ proper and $i,k$ open, put $W'=W\times_T S$, with projections $b:W'\to W$, $q:W'\to S$, and $s=(k,r):V\to W'$. The geometric clause of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] makes $s$ clopen. For varying coefficient sheaves let $\beta:p^*i_!\simeq b_!q^*$ be the open base-change identification: in the sheafified presheaf of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], a lift to $S$ is exactly a lift to $W'$. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] these open operations are exact. Project $q^*M$ onto its component on $s(V)$, apply $b_!$, and identify $b_!s_!=k_!$; this defines $a_Q:p^*i_!\to k_!r^*$. Define the actual derived tower map
$$\gamma_Q=(Rp_*k_!\varepsilon_r)\circ(Rp_*a_QRr_*)\circ(\eta_pi_!Rr_*):i_!Rr_*\longrightarrow Rp_*k_!.$$
Here the units, counits and the mate have the simultaneous section model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Evaluation is the finite proper/open mate, identified through the specified site comparisons with [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]; step 1 supplies its etale-origin hypotheses, so it is invertible by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. The coherence calculation also takes place before evaluation. On sheaf sections the maps $a_Q$ retain a summand exactly when its lift factors through the selected clopen component, and kill it otherwise. Two successive projections retain precisely the lifts retained by the pasted square; restriction and extension do not change their values. This verifies the pasted-$a$ identity for horizontal and vertical pasting, including refinement squares and identities, with the geometric clopen identifications in [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. This check uses only zero, identity, restriction and ring-linear projections, so applies unchanged to the ring system, not merely to constant-ring towers. [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] now gives the two proper/open pasting equations as equalities of actual derived tower transformations.

proof.text:
For $T\xrightarrow h B\xrightarrow g C$, choose a compatible tower of compactifications using [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. Write $i:B\hookrightarrow\overline B$, $q:\overline B\to C$, $a:T\hookrightarrow\overline T$, $p:\overline T\to\overline B$, and $U=\overline T\times_{\overline B}B$. Factor $a=bj$ with $j:T\hookrightarrow U$, $b:U\hookrightarrow\overline T$, and write $r:U\to B$ for the proper projection. Then the transformation
$$F_gF_h=Rq_*i_!Rr_*j_!\xrightarrow{Rq_*\gamma_Qj_!}Rq_*Rp_*b_!j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(qp)_*(bj)_!=F_{gh}$$
is defined in the tower derived category. The last arrow is the inverse of the canonical direct-image compositor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and the open compositor; the latter just composes the unique lifts in the extension presheaf. Refinement comparisons are the special cases of $\gamma$ with the left proper map an identity. By [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered] any two refinements have a common refinement and parallel arrows can be equalized; step 2's vertical and horizontal equations give the same comparison through that refinement. Any two compatible towers have a common refining tower by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]; apply the horizontal equation to its open strips and the vertical equation to its proper strips to obtain the commuting square between the two displayed composition maps. Thus it defines $\alpha_{g,h}$ for the chosen compactifications. For three maps, iterating this construction yields a staircase with two adjacent proper/open interchanges. The two parenthesizations are the two pastings of that staircase, hence are equal by those same two equations and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]; the direct-image compositors are the unit-preserving conjugates of pullback composition, so their associativity follows from the identity and pasting clauses of that node. Identity squares give identity maps. Evaluation gives exactly the finite construction of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], with the pro-etale normalization of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], so $\alpha$ is invertible. For an open $u$ take $(ju,p)$ as the compactification of $hu$ if $(j,p)$ compactifies $h$; $(ju)_!=j_!u_!$ on the extension presheaves gives $F_{hu}=F_hu_!$. The units include the unique lift and the counits evaluate that lift, so this identification respects the open counits. All restrictions land in the categories specified in the statement by its preservation assumption.

proof.text:
For etale $e:U\to T$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$. At each $n$ define $e_!M_n$ by sheafifying
$$V\longmapsto\bigoplus_{t:V\to U\,/T}M_n(V,t),$$
with transition maps induced on each summand by those of $M$. The scalar action factors through $A_n$, so this is an actual functor on varying-coefficient towers. [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] makes $e_!$ and $e^*$ exact; exactness on towers follows from [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. The unit places a section in the summand of its structural lift; the counit sums the evaluations of all lifts. Both commute with the quotient transitions summand by summand. The adjunction bijection is a bijection on compatible families because these unit/counit formulas are natural in the level maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] on complexes and then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]: exactness lets both functors descend, and the two triangle identities descend with them. This proves $e_{!,\bullet}\dashv e_\bullet^*$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories themselves, not by levelwise conservativity. For an open immersion there is at most one lift, giving extension by zero.

proof.text:
Identify this exact functor with the compactification candidate by constructing a comparison. For $e=pj$ and a pro-etale test scheme $V	o T$, a lift $t:V	o U$ determines a graph $V	o\overline U	imes_TV$. It is closed since $p$ is separated, and open since it lies in $U	imes_TV$ and is the pullback of the open diagonal of $e$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Extend a section in the $t$-summand by zero off this clopen graph. Summing the resulting sections and sheafifying defines $e_!M	o p_*j_!M$ naturally in $M$ and in its coefficient ring. On complexes compose this map with $p_*j_!M	o p_*I$, for a K-injective resolution $j_!M	o I$. The simultaneous construction of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] makes this an actual natural tower transformation $	heta:e_{!, ullet}	o F_e$. Its evaluation has exactly the inverse normalization of [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]: a section supported on a graph goes to that sheet. To compare sites, the exact functors $
u_T^*e_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $e_!^{\mathrm{proet}}
u_U^*$ have isomorphic right adjoints $e_{\mathrm{et}}^*
u_{T,*}\cong
u_{U,*}e_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. Their adjunction-preserving comparison is therefore an isomorphism on sheaves and, termwise, on complexes; its units include the structural summand and its counits sum the summands. Together with the specified compact-support site comparison [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], this identifies $	heta_n$ with the inverse finite normalization for the etale-origin levels of step 1. Hence $	heta$ is invertible by [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Use its inverse to identify $F_e$ with $e_{!, ullet}$ and the adjunction just constructed. [lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks] identifies its finite counit with the geometric fibre sum. The graph map and summand maps commute with coefficient quotient maps, and the last sum-extension identity of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] identifies that commutation with the named coefficient comparison. The open case uses the same unique-lift inclusion and evaluation.

proof.text:
Exactness of $e_!$ and $e^*$ gives $H^q(e_!M_n)=e_!H^q(M_n)$ and $H^q(e^*N_n)=e^*H^q(N_n)$, so each cohomological interval is preserved without shifting, uniformly in $n$. For every degree-zero module sheaf $N$ on $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] gives $e_!P\otimes N\cong e_!(P\otimes e^*N)$. It also shows that $e_!$ preserves flat sheaves: tensor an injection with a flat sheaf on $U$, then apply exact $e_!$. Thus applying this identity to K-flat resolutions gives
$$(e_!M_n)\otimes^LN\simeq e_!(M_n\otimes^Le^*N).$$
This preserves every Tor interval. For an arbitrary module sheaf $Q$ on $U$ the structural summand makes $Q$ a direct summand of $e^*e_!Q$: the complementary lifts are the complement of the clopen diagonal of separated $e$. For $L_n$ on $T$ with Tor interval $[a,b]$, $e^*L_n\otimes^LQ$ is a direct summand of
$$e^*(L_n\otimes^Le_!Q),$$
using derived tensor/pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The latter has the required interval by the Tor bound on $L_n$ and exactness of $e^*$, which proves it for $Q$. Constructibility for $e^*$ follows by pulling back the finite partition and the local constant finite presentations. Constructibility for $e_!$ on $\mathcal C_U$ follows from step 5 and the assumed preservation by $F_e$. The ambient adjunction therefore restricts to $\mathcal C_U,\mathcal C_T$ with precisely the same units and counits.

source.place: sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); the derived formula is obtained with flat resolutions. The diagonal summand gives the inverse-image Tor bound without a coefficient flatness assumption.

proof.text:
Let $t^C_{n,m}:C_n\to\operatorname{Res}_{n,m}C_m$ be the transition in restriction-of-scalars form; its scalar-adjunction transpose is $r^C_{n,m}$ [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. In the actual section model [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], the transition of the separately derived compact-support composite is
$$F_{h,n}C_n\xrightarrow{F_{h,n}(t^C_{n,m})}F_{h,n}\operatorname{Res}_{n,m}C_m\xrightarrow{d_h}\operatorname{Res}_{n,m}F_{h,m}C_m,$$
where $d_h$ is the canonical comparison of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. This concerns arbitrary strict transitions and does not require a normalized object. Take its transpose under scalar extension $-\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{n,m}$. The compatibility of the proper adjunction with restriction in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], and the coefficient projection clause of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], identify the transpose with
$$F_{h,m}(r^C_{n,m})\circ b_h(C_n).$$
In detail the proper factor is obtained by applying scalar extension to the $A_n$-counit and then taking its $A_m$-linear transpose; for the open factor tensor distributes over the defining extension presheaf, giving the extension-by-zero tensor comparison. These are exactly the specified factors of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], whose hypotheses apply to $C_n\in\Dctf$; in particular $b_h$ is invertible without $A_m$ being flat over $A_n$. This proves the displayed reduction identity for the actual transition, not for a newly chosen tower. For $n\geq m\geq r$, substitute this identity twice. Naturality of $b_{m,r}$ moves $F_{h,m}(r^C_{n,m})$ through it, and the coefficient-composition equation of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] replaces $b_{m,r}\circ(b_{n,m}\otimes^L A_r)$ by $b_{n,r}$ with the tensor associators. What remains inside $F_{h,r}$ is $r^C_{m,r}\circ(r^C_{n,m}\otimes^L A_r)$, equal to $r^C_{n,r}$ by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Naturality in $C$ follows by applying the same natural transformations to a tower morphism; for $m=n$ both the coefficient map and the scalar adjunction are identities.
